statement: Kernel-checked; advisory statement coverage and independent review remain open. For either sign s in {1,-1}, define the complete homogeneous odd-return operator on h modulo 3^r by L_s h(a)=sum_{k>=1} (3/2^k)*sum_{b mod 3^r, 2^k*a=3*b+s mod 3^(r+1)} h(b). The concrete branch congruence, uniqueness of the child at each exponent, nonnegative-row summability, zero nonunit output and sum_a L_s h(a)=3*sum_b h(b) are proved. For every r>=1 and fixed d>=1, if h vanishes on multiples of three and is positive on units, some unit residue a modulo 3^(r+d) satisfies L_s^d h(a)<h(a mod 3^r). The stronger form only requires h>=0 and h(-s)>0. The repeated k=1 branch gives L_s^d h(-s)>=(3/2)^d*h(-s), while both table sums equal 3^d*sum h. Actual-integer affine errors, deficient progressions, fate-class divergence and termination are outside this formal statement; no priority claim.
